data.name: Lehman Caves Visitor Center
data.description: Phone: (775) 234-7510 Lehman Caves Visitor Center is located 5.5 miles up from the town of Baker, NV. At this visitor center visitors can plan their visit, purchase cave tour tickets, watch the park movie, and explore exhibits about the caves and the darkness of Great Basin National Park.
data.audioDescription: Nestled at the base of the 13,000-foot South Snake Range, the Lehman Caves Visitor Center has fruit trees and large poplar trees close by. This brown building with a flat roof has double door entering into the information area and exhibit hall. To the left is the information desk and park store, to the right is the exhibit hall. The exhibit hall has two sections: caves and night skies. The cave section is a model of Lehman Caves with formations like shields, turnips, stalactites, and stalagmites. The night sky section has a curved ceiling with a large picture of the night sky at great basin with a timeline of different astronomical and historical events.

data.name: Great Basin Visitor Center
data.description: Phone: (775) 234-7520 Located just north of the town of Baker on the west side of NV Highway 487. The Visitor Center contains an information desk staffed by park rangers, exhibits about the ecology and history of the park, a theater with the park film, and brochures.
data.audioDescription: Located at the bottom of a valley. 13,000 foot mountains cover the background with colors changing from a sage green at the base to a treeless brown on the top of the peaks. The Visitor Center is tan with a sage green roof. There are two buildings with outdoor seating between them. Inside the Visitor Center, to the left is the park store, directly in font in the information desk, and to the right is the exhibit hall. Within the exhibit hall are numerous exhibits, starting on the left and moving in a clockwise motion. The exhibits cover the geology of the Great Basin, the night sky, bristle cone pine trees, life zones, and cultures of the Great Basin.
